messages.author: 0164fd77ac145c84
messages.subject: Multivariate Multiple Regression (multi_normal + wishart)
parts:
Hi!
I've been trying to get a multivariate regression to work in STAN, similar to the model depicted here in JAGS (http://jackman.stanford.edu/classes/BASS/92plain.bug) but with more dependent variables and using Wishart priors. This is the error message I get:

Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) :
  Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_cholesky_log(l): i and j must be same. Found i=235, j=3
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Below is the code. It runs ok if I replace the multi_normal in the likelihood with a regular normal or t distribution - then I adjust it to loop over the dependent variables and data points, and replace the Omega by a series of independent standard deviations obtained for each variable. I'm not sure what to try next. Any help to get this going would be much appreciated. I've attached a small chunk of the data if it helps.

Matt



MRegMod = '
  data {
    int<lower=1> nData;
    int<lower=1> nVars;
    real x3[nData];
    matrix[nData, nVars] y;
    matrix[nVars, nVars] Imat;
    vector[nVars] b0p;
    vector[nVars] b3p;
  }
  parameters {
    vector[nVars] b0;
    vector[nVars] b3;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega0;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega3;
    real<lower=0,upper=100> sd[nVars];
  }
  transformed parameters {
    matrix[nData, nVars] mu;
    for ( np in 1:nVars){
      for ( i in 1:nData){
        mu[i, np] <- b0[np] + b3[np] * x3[i];
      }
    }
  }

  model {
//Priors
    b0 ~ multi_normal(b0p , Omega0);
    b3 ~ multi_normal(b3p , Omega3);
    Omega0 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
    Omega3 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);

//Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nData){
      col(y, i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i), Omega);
    }
    Omega ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
  }
'

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate Multiple Regression (multi_normal + wishart)
parts: Hi Matt,

On Wednesday, January 30, 2013 6:54:30 AM UTC-5, Matt wrote:
I'm not sure what to try next. Any help to get this going would be much appreciated. I've attached a small chunk of the data if it helps.

What Marcus said should avoid the error message you got, but in general, calling multi_normal() (particularly repeatedly) is a slow process and to a lesser extent, so is inv_wishart(). The reason why this is sad but true is that these functions take a Cholesky factor and an inverse of their inputs every time the log-posterior is evaluated.

Thus, you would be better off

1) Calculating the Cholesky factor of Omega
2) Inverting it (i.e. doing a triangular solve with the identity matrix) and transposing

These two steps only have to be done once in the model block. Then for each variable ...

3) Premultiplying each column of y - mu by the result of 2)
4) Subtracting half the sum of squares of 3) from the log-posterior

There are some details in the Stan manual about this, particularly in the chapter entitled Optimizing Stan Code.

Ben

MRegMod = '
  data {
    int<lower=1> nData;
    int<lower=1> nVars;
    real x3[nData];
    matrix[nData, nVars] y;
    matrix[nVars, nVars] Imat;
    vector[nVars] b0p;
    vector[nVars] b3p;
  }
  parameters {
    vector[nVars] b0;
    vector[nVars] b3;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega0;
    cov_matrix[nVars] Omega3;
    real<lower=0,upper=100> sd[nVars];
  }
  transformed parameters {
    matrix[nData, nVars] mu;
    for ( np in 1:nVars){
      for ( i in 1:nData){
        mu[i, np] <- b0[np] + b3[np] * x3[i];
      }
    }
  }

  model {
//Priors
    b0 ~ multi_normal(b0p , Omega0);
    b3 ~ multi_normal(b3p , Omega3);
    Omega0 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
    Omega3 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);

//Likelihood
    for(i in 1:nData){
      col(y, i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i), Omega);

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Multivariate Multiple Regression (multi_normal + wishart)
parts:
Sorry -- those have to be vectors the way multi_normal
is currently defined.

You can look in the index of the manual to see the
signatures for which each function is defined.
You'll see that multi_normal is only defined for
vectors, not row vectors. So you can either
transpose (easy) or reorganize your data structures (more
efficient).

So
row(y, i) ~ multi_normal(row(mu,i), Omega);
should transpose the rows into (column) vectors:
row(y,i)' ~ multi_normal(row(mu,i)', Omega);

The more efficient approach would be to redefine
y to be an array of vectors, as in:

vector[???] y[nData];
vector[???] mu[nData];

y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Omega);

The advantage of this latter approach is that once we've
vectorized the multi_normal, you'll be able to write it
all without the loop as:

y ~ multi_normal(mu,Omega);

- Bob

On Friday, 1 February 2013 02:29:34 UTC+8, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Sorry -- those have to be vectors the way multi_normal
is currently defined.

You can look in the index of the manual to see the
signatures for which each function is defined.
You'll see that multi_normal is only defined for
vectors, not row vectors.  So you can either
transpose (easy) or reorganize your data structures (more
efficient).

So

   row(y, i) ~ multi_normal(row(mu,i), Omega);

should transpose the rows into (column) vectors:

   row(y,i)' ~ multi_normal(row(mu,i)', Omega);

The more efficient approach would be to redefine
y to be an array of vectors, as in:

   vector[???] y[nData];
   vector[???] mu[nData];

   y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Omega);

The advantage of this latter approach is that once we've
vectorized the multi_normal, you'll be able to write it
all without the loop as:

   y ~ multi_normal(mu,Omega);

- Bob
